html:
The Marri Ngarr are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory of Australia, in the coastal country southwest of Darwin, between the Daly River and Port Keats. The map shows them in 1600 and from 1715 to 1800.

Their language belongs to one of the small language families of the Daly River region, not to the Pama-Nyungan family of most of Australia. Many Marri Ngarr live today at Wadeye, the old Port Keats mission founded in 1935, alongside the Murrinh Patha and other peoples. Other neighbours on the map include the Marrithiyel and the Ngan'gi. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
